{"file_path": "/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c26_ec/plot_timeline.py", "content": """"Campaign 26 at 44 users in timeline.py's figures, as the earlier campaigns' sets. FIGSET picks the set:
  ec (default)  results/compare_c26_ec: every 44-user arm of the campaign with its controls and rivals
  designs       results/compare_c26_designs: original HiCache, the old oracle (v2), JIT p50, JIT exact and the pricing rules
In the container, from agent_cache/scripts/:
  [FIGSET=designs] PYTHONPATH=. python3 -B ../frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c26_ec/plot_timeline.py [labels ...]
Runs: the set's fixed runs of campaigns 21 and 23, its labels of campaign 26's manifest (ec: every 44-user one) and of
results/campaign26/extra_runs.txt. Per run: timeline_<label>.png, events_<label>.csv, turns_<label>.csv; labels on the
command line limit these to the runs named. Over the set's core arms, always: compare.png/.csv,
compare_steady_1800s.png/.csv, ttft_over_time_60s.png/.csv and paired_cdf_<label>.png (also _steady_1800s) against the
set's JIT p50. manifest.txt there lists label, run and client folder. A figure names a run "label (what it is)"; the CSVs
keep the label.
Colours of the core arms: plot_ec.py's six hues (pal.py on all pairs: worst dE 16.3 normal, 8.6 protan, 9.2 deutan), of
which designs takes five (the same worst pairs); the aqua is under 3:1 on the surface, so the CSVs are the table view."""
import csv, os, re, sys

import timeline

RES = "../results"
STEADY = 1800.0  # s, as the earlier sets' --steady-state
PAIRS = 2000  # pairs drawn per paired-CDF panel, as the earlier sets' --paired-max
BASELINE = "20261101_082229_three_tier_wc_custom_L1nat_H70"
WHAT = {"baseline": "original HiCache", "hintfree_ctl": "hint-free, read pins", "jit_p50_ctl": "JIT, p50 hints",
        "jit_p50_d": "JIT, p50 hints, new build", "jit_p50_d_cut": "JIT, p50 hints, new build, cut at minute 80 by the outage",
        "nofc_noend": "no hints, reads at arrival", "nofc": "no gap forecast, reads at arrival", "nofc_rep": "no gap forecast, repeat",
        "ec_r1": "rule 1 alone", "ec_r13": "rules 1 and 3", "ec_r13_rep": "rules 1 and 3, repeat", "ec_r3": "rule 3 alone, JIT p50 timing",
        "ec_r134": "rules 1, 3 and 4, learned price", "ec_full": "all four rules", "fq90": "JIT landing at the p90", "jit_exact": "JIT, exact hints",
        "jit_exact_d": "JIT, exact hints, new build", "oracle_v2": "old oracle v2, exact hints"}
# core: the arms compared, in the order of the legends and bars, with their colours. labels: campaign 26's manifest
# labels the set takes (None: every 44-user one). extra: its labels of extra_runs.txt.
SETS = {"ec": dict(out="compare_c26_ec", ref="jit_p50_ctl", labels=None, extra=("jit_p50_d_cut",), what={},
                   fixed={"baseline": BASELINE, "jit_exact": "20261101_202142_three_tier_wc_oracle_v2_nu_owned_custom_L1nat_H70"},
                   core={"baseline": "#2a78d6", "hintfree_ctl": "#796006", "jit_p50_ctl": "#a0307a", "nofc_noend": "#4a3aa7", "ec_r13": "#eb6834",
                         "jit_exact": "#1baf7a"}),
        # JIT and the rules on one build (engine_ec_20261111d), one run per arm; the other rule arms get timelines only.
        "designs": dict(out="compare_c26_designs", ref="jit_p50_d", extra=("oracle_v2",), fixed={"baseline": BASELINE},
                        labels=("jit_p50_d", "jit_exact_d", "ec_r1", "ec_r13", "ec_r13_rep", "ec_r134", "ec_full", "ec_r3"),
                        what={"jit_p50_d": "JIT, p50 hints", "jit_exact_d": "JIT, exact hints"},
                        core={"baseline": "#2a78d6", "oracle_v2": "#4a3aa7", "jit_p50_d": "#a0307a", "jit_exact_d": "#1baf7a", "ec_r13": "#eb6834"})}
SET = SETS[os.environ.get("FIGSET", "ec")]
OUT, REF, CORE = os.path.join(RES, SET["out"]), SET["ref"], SET["core"]
WHAT = WHAT | SET["what"]
name = lambda label: f"{label} ({WHAT[label]})" if label in WHAT else label
last_client = lambda run: sorted(d for d in os.listdir(os.path.join(RES, run)) if d.startswith("client_"))[-1]

runs = {label: (run, last_client(run)) for label, run in SET["fixed"].items()}
for f in (line.split() for line in open(os.path.join(RES, "campaign26", "manifest.txt"))):
    # Arms of another setting (128 users, another host pool) are drawn only when named.
    if f and (f[0] in SET["labels"] if SET["labels"] else f[0] in sys.argv[1:] or not (f[0].endswith("_c128") or re.search(r"_h\d+$", f[0]))):
        runs[f[0]] = (f[1], f[2])
extra = os.path.join(RES, "campaign26", "extra_runs.txt")
for f in (line.split() for line in (open(extra) if os.path.exists(extra) else ()) if line.strip() and not line.startswith("#")):
    if f[0] in SET["extra"]:
        runs[f[0]] = (f[1], last_client(f[1]))
runs = {label: runs[label] for label in (*(a for a in CORE if a in runs), *(a for a in runs if a not in CORE))}
asked = sys.argv[1:]
unknown = [a for a in asked if a not in runs]
if unknown:
    sys.exit(f"not a run of this set: {', '.join(unknown)} (have {', '.join(runs)})")
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
with open(os.path.join(OUT, "manifest.txt"), "w") as f:
    for label, (run, client) in runs.items():
        f.write(f"{label} {run} {client}\n")

parsed = {}
for label, (run, client) in runs.items():
    draw = not asked or label in asked
    if not draw and label not in CORE:
        continue
    cl = timeline.parse_client(os.path.join(RES, run, client, "client.jsonl"), "private")
    sv = timeline.parse_server(os.path.join(RES, run, "server.log"), cl["t_start"], {t["rid"]: t["t0"] for t in cl["turns"]})
    m = timeline.arm_metrics(name(label), cl, sv)
    if draw:
        timeline.draw_timeline(name(label), cl, sv, os.pat

# Redraws results/compare_c26_designs: 44 users, 70 GB, 0.1 users/s; original HiCache, the old oracle (v2), JIT p50,
# JIT exact and the pricing rules. From the host:
#   docker exec sglang_hicache bash /sgl-workspace/sglang/agent_cache/frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c26_ec/figs_designs.sh
# Rule arms join their timelines and the wait split as they land in results/campaign26/manifest.txt.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=/sgl-workspace/sglang/agent_cache
HERE=$ROOT/frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c26_ec
OUT=results/compare_c26_designs
# No GPU for the plots: a campaign may be running on it.
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 FIGSET=designs PYTHONPATH=$ROOT/scripts

cd $ROOT/scripts
nice -n 15 python3 -B $HERE/plot_timeline.py
nice -n 15 python3 -B $HERE/plot_pricing_vs_jit.py --set designs 2> >(grep -v findfont >&2)
nice -n 15 python3 -B $HERE/plot_ec.py

cd $ROOT
RULES=""
for arm in ec_r1 ec_r3 ec_r13 ec_r13_rep ec_r134 ec_full; do
    if grep -q "^$arm " results/campaign26/manifest.txt; then RULES="$RULES $arm"; fi
done
STALL_CSV=$OUT/ec_wait_split.csv nice -n 15 python3 -I -B $HERE/stall_ec.py baseline oracle_v2 jit_p50_d jit_exact_d $RULES > results/campaign26/stall_ec_designs.out
cd $ROOT/scripts
nice -n 15 python3 -B $HERE/plot_stall.py ../$OUT/ec_wait_split.csv
"}

"""Where a returning turn's TTFT goes once the cache policy has done its part: before the scheduler sees the request, in its queue, after admission."""
import glob, json, os, re, statistics as st, sys

RES = "results"
RTS = re.compile(r"ReqTimeStats\(rid=\S+?-c(\d+)-t(\d+), input_len=(\d+), cached_input_len=(\d+), output_len=(\d+).*queue_duration=([\d.]+)ms, forward_duration=([\d.]+)ms, entry_time=([\d.]+)")
pct = lambda v, q: sorted(v)[min(len(v) - 1, int(q * len(v)))] if v else float("nan")
for run in sys.argv[1:]:
    path = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(RES, run, "client_*", "client.jsonl")))[-1]
    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(path) if l.strip()]
    t0 = next(r["t_start"] for r in rows if r["kind"] == "run")
    turns = {(r["conv"], r["turn"]): r for r in rows if r["kind"] == "turn" and r.get("ttft") is not None}
    srv = {}
    for line in open(os.path.join(RES, run, "server.log"), errors="replace"):
        if "ReqTimeStats(" in line and (m := RTS.search(line)):
            srv[(int(m[1]), int(m[2]))] = dict(inp=int(m[3]), cached=int(m[4]), out=int(m[5]), queue=float(m[6]) / 1000, fwd=float(m[7]) / 1000, entry=float(m[8]))
    rec = []
    for k, r in turns.items():
        if k[1] == 0 or r.get("mid_start") or k not in srv:
            continue
        s = srv[k]
        cd = r.get("cached_details") or {}
        pre = s["entry"] - (t0 + r["t_send"])
        tier = "storage" if (cd.get("storage") or 0) > 0 else "host" if (cd.get("host") or 0) > 0 else "device"
        rec.append(dict(pre=pre, queue=s["queue"], after=r["ttft"] - pre - s["queue"], ttft=r["ttft"], prompt=s["inp"], new=s["inp"] - s["cached"], tier=tier,
                        host=int(cd.get("host") or 0), storage=int(cd.get("storage") or 0), t=r["t_send"]))
    n = len(rec)
    mean = lambda key, rs=rec: st.mean(x[key] for x in rs)
    print(f"\n{run}: {n} returning turns with server stats")
    print(f"  mean TTFT {mean('ttft'):.3f} = before entry {mean('pre'):.3f} + scheduler queue {mean('queue'):.3f} + after admission {mean('after'):.3f}")
    print(f"  median TTFT {st.median(x['ttft'] for x in rec):.3f}; before entry median {st.median(x['pre'] for x in rec):.3f} p90 {pct([x['pre'] for x in rec], .9):.3f}; "
          f"after admission median {st.median(x['after'] for x in rec):.3f} p90 {pct([x['after'] for x in rec], .9):.3f}")
    print("  before entry by prompt length (tokens): n, median s, mean s")
    for lo, hi in ((0, 8000), (8000, 16000), (16000, 32000), (32000, 64000), (64000, 200000)):
        v = [x["pre"] for x in rec if lo <= x["prompt"] < hi]
        if v:
            print(f"    {lo:6d}-{hi:6d}: {len(v):5d} {st.median(v):.3f} {st.mean(v):.3f}")
    print("  after admission by where the prefix was, turns with no queue wait over 50 ms: n, median s, mean s, mean new tokens, mean tokens loaded from host or storage")
    calm = [x for x in rec if x["queue"] < 0.05]
    for tier in ("device", "host", "storage"):
        v = [x for x in calm if x["tier"] == tier]
        if v:
            print(f"    {tier:8s} {len(v):5d} {st.median(x['after'] for x in v):.3f} {mean('after', v):.3f} {mean('new', v):7.0f} {st.mean(x['host'] + x['storage'] for x in v):8.0f}")
    print("  device-prefix turns with no queue wait, after admission by new tokens: n, median s")
    dev = [x for x in calm if x["tier"] == "device"]
    for lo, hi in ((0, 128), (128, 512), (512, 2048), (2048, 8192), (8192, 10**6)):
        v = [x["after"] for x in dev if lo <= x["new"] < hi]
        if v:
            print(f"    {lo:5d}-{hi:7d}: {len(v):5d} {st.median(v):.3f}")
    print(f"  share of all TTFT seconds: before entry {sum(x['pre'] for x in rec) / sum(x['ttft'] for x in rec):.0%}, queue {sum(x['queue'] for x in rec) / sum(x['ttft'] for x in rec):.0%}, "
          f"after admission {sum(x['after'] for x in rec) / sum(x['ttft'] for x in rec):.0%}")
EOF

{"command": "cat > /tmp/claude-1001/-home-wanhr-sglang/7c93b1d5-dc1c-431d-8d3e-efb4ae23a30d/scratchpad/why_recompute.py <<'EOF'
"""For the returning turns that computed 4K+ tokens of history again: what the server did for them before admission."""
import collections, glob, json, os, re, statistics as st, sys

RES = "results"
RID = r"(?:rid|req)=\S+?-c(\d+)-t(\d+)"
PATS = {"query": re.compile(r"HICACHE_EVT s2h_query " + RID + r" tokens_req=(\d+) storage_hit=(\d+)"),
        "dispatch": re.compile(r"HICACHE_EVT srs_dispatch " + RID + r" pages=(\d+) .*launched=(\d)"),
        "io": re.compile(r"HICACHE_EVT s2h_io " + RID + r" pages=(\d+)"),
        "success": re.compile(r"HiCache prefetch success " + RID + r" completed=(\d+) matched=(\d+) loaded=(\d+)"),
        "shrank": re.compile(r"device prefix shrank before admission " + RID + r" lookup_match=(\d+) current_match=(\d+)"),
        "start": re.compile(r"HICACHE_EVT prefetch_start " + RID + r" tokens=(\d+)"),
        "unpin": re.compile(r"HICACHE_EVT srs_unpin " + RID + r" tokens=(\d+) reason=(\w+)")}
for run in sys.argv[1:]:
    path = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(RES, run, "client_*", "client.jsonl")))[-1]
    rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(path) if l.strip()]
    rec = lambda r: max(r.get("reply_reprefilled") or 0, 0)
    big = {(r["conv"], r["turn"]): r for r in rows if r["kind"] == "turn" and r.get("ttft") is not None and r["turn"] > 0 and not r.get("mid_start") and rec(r) >= 4096}
    ev = collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(list))
    for line in open(os.path.join(RES, run, "server.log"), errors="replace"):
        if "-c" not in line:
            continue
        for name, pat in PATS.items():
            if m := pat.search(line):
                k = (int(m[1]), int(m[2]))
                if k in big:
                    ev[k][name].append(m.groups()[2:])
                break
    cats = collections.Counter()
    tok = collections.Counter()
    detail = []
    for k, r in big.items():
        e = ev[k]
        hit = max((int(h) for _, h in e["query"]), default=0)
        refused = sum(1 for _, launched in e["dispatch"] if launched == "0")
        read_tokens = 64 * sum(int(p[0]) for p in e["io"])
        loaded = sum(int(l) for _, _, l in e["success"])
        if not e["query"] and not e["start"]:
            cat = "no SSD lookup at all"
        elif hit == 0:
            cat = "looked up, nothing on SSD"
        elif e["shrank"] or any(reason != "admit" for _, reason in e["unpin"]):
            cat = "read, then lost before admission"
        elif refused and read_tokens < 0.5 * rec(r):
            cat = "read refused room"
        elif read_tokens < 0.5 * hit:
            cat = "found on SSD, read little"
        else:
            cat = "read most of what SSD had; SSD had less than the history"
        cats[cat] += 1
        tok[cat] += rec(r)
        detail.append((cat, rec(r), hit, read_tokens, refused, r["ttft"]))
    n, total = len(big), sum(tok.values())
    print(f"\n{run}: {n} returning turns recomputed 4K+ tokens ({total / 1e6:.2f}M tokens)")
    for cat, c in cats.most_common():
        d = [x for x in detail if x[0] == cat]
        print(f"  {cat:58s} {c:4d} turns, {tok[cat] / total:4.0%} of those tokens; recomputed median {st.median(x[1] for x in d):6.0f}, SSD hit median {st.median(x[2] for x in d):6.0f}, "
              f"read median {st.median(x[3] for x in d):6.0f}, refusals mean {st.mean(x[4] for x in d):.1f}, TTFT mean {st.mean(x[5] for x in d):5.1f} s")
EOF

**What still limits the best arms (${NOW} on 2026-11-12, asked for; scripts and outputs in \`checks/limits/\`).** Whole
runs of \`jit_exact_d\` and \`nofc_noend\`, returning turns. Mean TTFT of \`jit_exact_d\` 0.82 s (median 0.27 s) = 0.14 s
before the scheduler has the request + 0.38 s in its queue + 0.29 s after admission.

- **One turn in a hundred computes its history again, and that is the largest loss left.** 123 returning turns (1.0 %)
  recompute 4K tokens or more: 11.1 s mean TTFT against 0.71 s for the rest, 14 % of all TTFT seconds, and 2.6M
  tokens, 23 % of the run's prefill work, 72 % of them in the fourteen worst minutes. \`nofc_noend\`: 113 turns, 2.4M
  tokens, 22 %.
- **Their history was on SSD and host memory had no room for it.** Of the 123: 58 had the read refused room and read
  nothing (58 % of the tokens; median 20K tokens on SSD, 2.1 refusals), 25 read it and lost it before admission
  (21 %), 31 read less than the history (11 %). \`nofc_noend\`: 50, 22 and 34. The room beyond the GPU's copy is 44K
  tokens, about two such histories. No staged read is involved in \`nofc_noend\`, so rule 2 cannot be what frees it:
  staged pins hold 2-6K tokens on average.
- **The queue is fourteen minutes.** They hold 89 % of \`jit_exact_d\`'s queue seconds (65 % of \`nofc_noend\`'s): minutes
  53-62, 86-91 and 116-119, GPU pool 0.8-0.96 full, 3-9 turns a minute with 8K or more tokens to prefill against
  0.7 otherwise. Outside them \`nofc_noend\` queues 24 s a minute against 6 s: its reads at arrival, which is what
  exact hints save.
- **Before the scheduler:** median 0.08 s, mean 0.14 s, growing with the prompt (0.04 s under 8K tokens, 0.11 s at
  32-64K, 0.17 s above); 17 % of all TTFT seconds. Not profiled; the server tokenizes the whole history each turn
  with one tokenizer worker.
- **After admission:** 0.14 s with under 128 new tokens, 0.23 s at 512-2K, 0.51 s at 2-8K. A prefix loaded from host
  costs 5-45 ms more than one on the GPU, so staging onto the GPU would buy little.
- **Decode:** 37, 49 and 62 ms a step at 8-15, 16-23 and 24-31 running requests, so going from about 20 to 28 running
  adds about 11 % tokens per second while holding 40 % more of the GPU pool.

Read: the next gain at this setting is room for an arrived turn's read (the host pool mirrors the GPU, so 668K of
its 712K tokens are copies of what the GPU holds), not the timing of early reads. The 100 GB arms (room 349K) are the
first test; \`PAPER_PLAN.md\` item 4 already names the mirror.
EOF

stamp = lambda s: dt.datetime.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f").replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc).timestamp()

    by = collections.defaultdict(list)

print("minute | learned price: price, refused K in the minute, idle room K, staged pins K, harm s | fixed price run: refused K, idle room K, staged pins K, harm s")

"""Start decisions and price log of one run's server.log (path in argv[1]); client start in argv[2] as HH:MM:SS UTC."""
import re, statistics as st, sys
from datetime import datetime

log, t0s = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
stamp = lambda line: datetime.strptime(line[1:24], "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f")
rows, prices, t0 = [], [], None
for line in open(log, errors="replace"):
    if "HICACHE_EVT ec_start" in line:
        kv = dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in line.split("ec_start", 1)[1].split())
        rows.append((stamp(line), kv))
    elif "HICACHE_EVT ec_price" in line:
        prices.append((stamp(line), line.split("ec_price", 1)[1].strip()))
day = rows[0][0].strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
t0 = datetime.strptime(f"{day} {t0s}", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
q = lambda v, p: sorted(v)[min(len(v) - 1, int(p * len(v)))]
for d in sorted({kv["decision"] for _, kv in rows}):
    sub = [(t, kv) for t, kv in rows if kv["decision"] == d]
    read = [float(kv["read_ms"]) / 1000 for _, kv in sub]
    wait = [float(kv["wait_ms"]) / 1000 for _, kv in sub]
    tok = [int(kv["tokens"]) for _, kv in sub]
    ts = [(t - t0).total_seconds() for t, _ in sub]
    print(f"{d:8s} n {len(sub):5d} | at {min(ts):7.0f}-{max(ts):7.0f} s | read s p10 {q(read, .1):.2f} p50 {q(read, .5):.2f} p90 {q(read, .9):.2f} max {max(read):.2f} | "
          f"queue wait s p10 {q(wait, .1):.2f} p50 {q(wait, .5):.2f} p90 {q(wait, .9):.2f} min {min(wait):.2f} | tokens p50 {q(tok, .5)} p90 {q(tok, .9)} | "
          f"read < wait in {sum(r < w for r, w in zip(read, wait))}")
print("first decision at", f"{(rows[0][0] - t0).total_seconds():.0f} s; decisions before 6900 s:", sum((t - t0).total_seconds() < 6900 for t, _ in rows))
print("price events", len(prices), "| first", prices[0][1][:200])
print("last ", prices[-1][1][:200])
vals = [float(m.group(1)) for _, p in prices if (m := re.search(r"price=([0-9.e+-]+)", p))]
print("price min", min(vals), "max", max(vals), "distinct", sorted(set(vals))[:8])
EOF

    '    if any(a.key.startswith("nofc") for a in arms):\n')
open(p, "w").write(s)

p = "plot_stall.py"

sub('    NOTE = ("A just-in-time read is timed to land as its turn is admitted, so in those arms the wait for the read is queue time the turn had anyway.\\n"\n'

sub('    NOTE = NOTE.format(hinted=', '    NOTE = NOTE.format(priced=PRICED if any(r["arm"].startswith("ec_") for r in rows) else "", hinted=')

"""ntp_hold lines of one or more runs' server.log: how long an arrived turn's read was held, against its wait and load."""
import sys

q = lambda v, p: sorted(v)[min(len(v) - 1, int(p * len(v)))]

          f"expected wait s p50 {q(wait, .5):5.1f} | load s p50 {q(load, .5):4.1f} p90 {q(load, .9):4.1f}")
EOF

early, and the arm lands with the old oracle.** Tables: `compare_c128.out` (eight runs; the seven-run table is kept as
`compare_c128_7runs.out`), `stall_ec_designs_c128.out`. Each run's first 6,900 s; one run per arm, no repeat at 128 users.

| First 6,900 s | HiCache | old oracle | old p50 | JIT exact | JIT p50 | no hints | rules 1, 3, 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| turns | 8,334 | 15,525 | 15,473 | 15,384 | 15,366 | 15,418 | 15,502 |
| mean TTFT, all turns | 50.20 s | 20.58 s | 20.68 s | 20.93 s | 20.98 s | 20.84 s | 20.57 s |
| mean TTFT, 8,001 shared returning turns | 50.55 s | 11.73 s | 11.82 s | 12.12 s | 12.23 s | 12.07 s | 11.70 s |
| turn latency on them | 74.67 s | 23.67 s | 23.78 s | 24.18 s | 24.32 s | 24.13 s | 23.64 s |
| SSD pages | 433K | 1,438K | 1,441K | 998K | 1,195K | 1,153K | 1,049K |
| returning turns reading from SSD | 19.6 % | 33.1 % | 32.7 % | 21.4 % | 25.5 % | 25.9 % | 23.6 % |
| turns with over one read | 1 | 36 | 162 | 0 | 120 | 0 | 0 |
| reads staged before arrival | 0 | 4,643 | 4,556 | 2 | 462 | 0 | 0 |

- **Clean.** 16,227 turns in the 2 h, no client errors, no tracebacks, settings as queued (expected cost, 5e-5, price
  learning `harm`, soft pins off, return chance with a 30 s horizon).
- **Rule 1 started no read early, so rule 4 had nothing to learn from.** 3,670 start decisions from 2,073 s on, every one

{"file_path": "/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/campaign26/checks/read_starts.py", "content": """"When a pricing arm starts its SSD reads: rule 1's start decisions, the price log and the hold on arrived turns' reads.
From agent_cache/:  nice -n 10 python3 -I -B results/campaign26/checks/read_starts.py label=run [label=run ...]
Per run, from server.log's ec_start, ec_price and ntp_hold lines: the decisions by kind (now: read started before its
turn arrived; wait: timed for later; arrival: left to the turn's arrival) with the estimates they were taken on; the
price's range with the most tokens read pins held, staged and refused and the harm charged; the reads held after
arrival. Times are seconds since the client started. A run without pricing prints its holds only."""
import datetime as dt, json, os, re, sys

TS = re.compile(r"^\[(.{23})\] HICACHE_EVT (ec_start|ec_price|ntp_hold) (.*)")
stamp = lambda s: dt.datetime.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f").replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc).timestamp()
q = lambda v, p: sorted(v)[min(len(v) - 1, int(p * len(v)))]
fields = lambda text: dict(part.split("=", 1) for part in text.split() if "=" in part)

for name, run in (a.split("=") for a in sys.argv[1:]):
    client = sorted(d for d in os.listdir(f"results/{run}") if d.startswith("client_"))[-1]
    rows = (json.loads(line) for line in open(f"results/{run}/{client}/client.jsonl") if line.strip())
    t_start = next(r["t_start"] for r in rows if r.get("kind") == "run")
    starts, prices, holds = [], [], []
    for line in open(f"results/{run}/server.log", errors="replace"):
        m = TS.match(line)
        if m:
            {"ec_start": starts, "ec_price": prices, "ntp_hold": holds}[m.group(2)].append((stamp(m.group(1)) - t_start, fields(m.group(3))))
    print(f"{name} {run}")
    for kind in sorted({kv["decision"] for _, kv in starts}):
        sub = [(t, kv) for t, kv in starts if kv["decision"] == kind]
        read, wait = ([float(kv[k]) / 1000 for _, kv in sub] for k in ("read_ms", "wait_ms"))
        print(f"  start {kind:8s} {len(sub):5d} at {min(t for t, _ in sub):5.0f}-{max(t for t, _ in sub):5.0f} s | read s p10 p50 p90 {q(read, .1):5.2f} "
              f"{q(read, .5):5.2f} {q(read, .9):5.2f} | queue wait after arrival s {q(wait, .1):5.2f} {q(wait, .5):5.2f} {q(wait, .9):5.2f} | "
              f"read shorter than the wait in {sum(r < w for r, w in zip(read, wait))}")
    if prices:
        col = lambda k: [float(kv[k]) for _, kv in prices]
        print(f"  price lines {len(prices)}: price {min(col('price')):.3g} to {max(col('price')):.3g} | most tokens held by read pins {max(col('held')):.0f}, "
              f"staged {max(col('staged')):.0f}, refused {max(col('refused')):.0f} | harm charged {sum(col('harm_ms')) / 1000:.1f} s | "
              f"room at the end {prices[-1][1]['room']}")
    if holds:
        held, wait, load = ([float(kv[k]) / 1000 for _, kv in holds] for k in ("hold_ms", "wait_ms", "load_ms"))
        print(f"  reads held after arrival {len(holds)}: held s p10 p50 p90 {q(held, .1):5.1f} {q(held, .5):5.1f} {q(held, .9):5.1f} | expected wait s p50 "
              f"{q(wait, .5):5.1f} | load estimate s p50 p90 {q(load, .5):5.1f} {q(load, .9):5.1f}")
"}

input:
{"file_path": "/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/campaign26/checks/bumps.py", "content": """"Rule 2 (soft pins): what the bumped staged reads cost, and what the turns they made room for got.
From agent_cache/:  nice -n 10 python3 -I -B results/campaign26/checks/bumps.py label=run [reference=run]
An ec_bump line is a staged read given up so that the read of a turn that has arrived finds room. For the first run:
the bumps and the SSD pages their reads had loaded, when the bumped turns arrived and whether they read again, and the
SSD pages by what became of the read. With a reference run (the same arm without soft pins): TTFT of the bumped
turns, of the turns the room went to and of the other returning turns, beside the same turns there.
Times are seconds; a turn is a (user, turn) pair, and only turns both runs recorded are set side by side."""
import collections, datetime as dt, json, os, re, statistics as st, sys

EVT = re.compile(r"^\[(.{23})\] HICACHE_EVT (ec_bump|s2h_io|ntp_arrive|ntp_stage) rid=\S+?-c(\d+)-t(\d+)(.*)")
FOR = re.compile(r"for_rid=\S+?-c(\d+)-t(\d+) tokens=(\d+) chance=([\d.]+)")
PAGES = re.compile(r"pages=(\d+)")
stamp = lambda s: dt.datetime.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f").replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc).timestamp()
q = lambda v, p: sorted(v)[min(len(v) - 1, int(p * len(v)))] if v else float("nan")
three = lambda v: f"{q(v, .1):.1f} {q(v, .5):.1f} {q(v, .9):.1f}"


def turns(run):
    """(user, turn) -> the client's record, for the turns that got a first token."""
    client = sorted(d for d in os.listdir(f"results/{run}") if d.startswith("client_"))[-1]
    rows = (json.loads(line) for line in open(f"results/{run}/{client}/client.jsonl") if line.strip())
    return {(r["conv"], r["turn"]): r for r in rows if r.get("kind") == "turn" and r.get("ttft") is not None}


def beside(name, keys, own, other):
    """Mean TTFT of the keys in the run, and against the reference on the keys both have."""
    have = [k for k in keys if k in own]
    line = f"  {name}: {len(have)} turns, mean TTFT {st.mean(own[k]['ttft'] for k in have):.2f} s, median {st.median(own[k]['ttft'] for k in have):.2f}"
    both = [k for k in have if k in other]
    if both:
        d = [own[k]["ttft"] - other[k]["ttft"] for k in both]
        line += (f" | on the {len(both)} also in the reference: {st.mean(own[k]['ttft'] for k in both):.2f} s against {st.mean(other[k]['ttft'] for k in both):.2f} s, "
                 f"paired {st.mean(d):+.3f} s (faster on {sum(x < -0.05 for x in d)}, slower on {sum(x > 0.05 for x in d)})")
    print(line)


(name, run), ref = sys.argv[1].split("="), (sys.argv[2].split("=") if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None)
bumps, arrive = [], {}
reads, stages = collections.defaultdict(list), collections.Counter()
for line in open(f"results/{run}/server.log", errors="replace"):
    m = EVT.match(line)
    if not m:
        continue
    t, kind, key = stamp(m.group(1)), m.group(2), (int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4)))
    if kind == "ec_bump":
        f = FOR.search(m.group(5))
        bumps.append((t, key, (int(f.group(1)), int(f.group(2))), int(f.group(3)), float(f.group(4))))
    elif kind == "s2h_io":
        reads[key].append((t, int(PAGES.search(m.group(5)).group(1))))
    elif kind == "ntp_arrive":
        arrive[key] = t
    else:
        stages[key] += 1
own = turns(run)
total = sum(p for v in reads.values() for _, p in v)
per_turn = collections.Counter(key for _, key, *_ in bumps)
print(f"{name} {run}")
print(f"  bumps {len(bumps)} of {sum(stages.values())} staged reads, on {len(per_turn)} turns ({sum(n > 1 for n in per_turn.values())} bumped more than once), "
      f"for {len({b[2] for b in bumps})} arrived turns; tokens given up {sum(b[3] for b in bumps):,} (median {st.median(b[3] for b in bumps):.0f} per bump); "
      f"chance of return within the read time p10 p50 p90 {q([b[4] for b in bumps], .1):.2f} {q([b[4] for b in bumps], .5):.2f} {q([b[4] for b in bumps], .9):.2f}")

# A read belongs to the bump that follows it: the pages it loaded were given up.
lost, sat, gap, late = 0, [], [], collections.Counter()
for t, key, _, _, _ in bumps:
    before = [(at, p) for at, p in reads[key] if at <= t]
    if before:
        lost += before[-1][1]
        sat.append(t - before[-1][0])
    after = [at for at, _ in reads[key] if at > t]
    if key not in arrive:
        late["never arrived"] += 1
        continue
    gap.append(arrive[key] - t)
    late["read again before arrival" if any(at <= arrive[key] for at in after) else "read at arrival" if after else "no further read"] += 1
print(f"  SSD pages their reads had loaded: {lost:,} ({100 * lost / total:.1f} % of the run's {total:,}); the data had sat {three(sat)} s (p10 p50 p90) when bumped")
print(f"  bump to the turn's arrival {three(gap)} s; within 1 s {sum(g <= 1 for g in gap)}, within 5 s {sum(g <= 5 for g in gap)} of {len(gap)}; afterwards: "
      + ", ".join(f"{k} {n}" for k, n in late.most_common()))

# Every read of the run by what became of it.
fate = collections.Counter()
for key, v in reads.items():
    cut = sorted(t for t, k, *_ in bumps if k == key)
    for at, p in v:
        staged = key not in arrive or at <= arrive[key]
        fate["at or after arrival" if not staged else "staged, then bumped" if any(t >= at for t in cut) else "staged and kept"] += p
print("  SSD pages by read: " + ", ".join(f"{k} {n:,} ({100 * n / total:.0f} %)" for k, n in fate.most_common()))

other = turns(ref[1]) if ref else {}
if ref:
    print(f"  reference {ref[0]} {ref[1]}")
bumped, helped = set(per_turn), {b[2] for b in bumps}
beside("bumped turns", bumped, own, other)
beside("turns the room went to", helped - bumped, own, other)
beside("other returning turns", {k for k in own if k[1] > 0} - bumped - helped, own, oth

{"command": "cd /home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache; cat >> results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md <<'EOF'

**`ec_full` (done 23:53Z on 2026-11-12, clean, GPU unit `GPU-6374d407`): all four rules land at 0.66 s, the best
pricing run's level; rule 2 does what it was built to do and pays for it in SSD traffic.** Tables: `compare_ec.out`
(18 runs), `pairs_ec.out` (11 leading runs; earlier `pairs_ec_10runs.out`), `pairs_ec_ctl.out` (18 runs; earlier
`pairs_ec_ctl_17runs.out`), `stall_ec_designs.out`, `checks/latency_lead11.out`, `checks/read_starts_c44.out`,
`checks/bumps.out`. One run of this arm.

| 6,715 shared returning turns | JIT exact | rules 1, 3 | rule 1 | rules 1, 3, 4 | all four | no gap forecast | no hints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean TTFT | 0.51, 0.54 s | 0.66, 0.78 s | 0.67 s | 0.80 s | 0.66 s | 0.69, 0.80 s | 0.71, 0.72 s |
| in the two load episodes | 1.14, 1.31 s | 1.56, 2.31 s | 1.75 s | 2.22 s | 1.66 s | 1.83, 2.21 s | 1.85, 1.84 s |
| turns over 10 s | 14, 27 | 30, 93 | 55 | 83 | 38 | 53, 66 | 25, 47 |
| recomputed tokens per turn | 120, 151 | 214, 253 | 181 | 320 | 169 | 131, 193 | 145, 135 |
| SSD pages, whole run | 388K, 397K | 437K, 415K | 448K | 420K | 534K | 469K, 482K | 562K, 559K |
| reads started before arrival | 1,202, 1,207 | 629, 560 | 669 | 838 | 1,566 | 0 | 0 |
| turns sent before minute 115 | 11,699, 11,703 | 11,690, 11,527 | 11,580 | 11,446 | 11,706 | 11,710, 11,654 | 11,680, 11,645 |

- **Clean.** 12,161 turns in the 2 h, no client errors, no tracebacks, settings as queued (expected cost, 5e-5, price
  learning `harm`, soft pins on, return chance with a 30 s horizon). Decode, first-turn prefill and SSD speed in line
  with the other arms (37.2 ms per step at 8-15 running, 0.089 ms per token, 2.34 ms per page).
- **Rule 2 works as built.** With soft pins an arrived turn's read takes room from staged reads instead of being
  refused. The harm charged to early reads fell from 1,081 s (`ec_r134`) to 404 s, so the learned price settled lower
  (median 1.4e-5 against 3.1e-5, from 5e-5), and rule 1 started 1,566 reads early against 838.
- **It pays in SSD traffic.** 462 of the 1,569 staged reads were bumped (352 turns, 110 of them more than once, for 301
  arrived turns). Their reads had loaded 81K pages, 14 % of all the run read and 47 % of what it staged. The data had
  sat a median 2.4 s; the bumped turn arrived a median 8.4 s later (163 of 462 within 5 s) and 452 read again, 192
  before arrival and 260 at it. Whole run: 534K pages, 27 % over `ec_r134`, 22-29 % over rules 1 and 3, 5 % under the
  no-hint arm (the fixed-price rules were 22-26 % under it). SSD reads used: 72 % (88-89 % in the other pricing arms).
- **No more turns found their read landed.** On the 7,283 turns the designs share: 196 of 1,049 reading turns had
  landed by arrival, against 206 of 988 (`ec_r134`) and 130-134 (rules 1 and 3); JIT exact 442 of 740. Its wait is
  0.65 s = 0.17 read stall + 0.08 other queue wait + 0.39 after admission; `ec_r134` 0.77 = 0.18 + 0.15 + 0.44.
- **TTFT: nothing shown beyond what the pricing arms already had.** Against `ec_r134` -0.14 s on the 6,715 turns (5 %
  to 95 %: -0.25 to -0.04) and -0.09 s on the 11,067 (-0.21 to +0.05), one run each, where a rerun of rules 1 and 3
  moved 0.12 and 0.10 s. The gain is not on the turns the bumps touched: bumped turns +0.06 s (339 turns), turns the
  room went to +0.18 s (217), all other returning turns -0.12 s (10,936). Against rules 1 and 3 it is inside their two
  runs (+0.00 and -0.12 s). Ahead of the no-hint arm in both pairs (0.05-0.06 s; 0.11 s on the 11,067), behind exact
  hints in both (0.12-0.15 s; 0.03-0.10 s); with no repeat of this arm neither counts as shown.
- **Latency and throughput: level with the best.** 12.03 s per turn on the 11,067 (exact hints 12.08 and 12.06 s, no
  hints 12.12 and 12.17 s, `ec_r134` 12.67 s) and 11,706 turns before minute 115.
- **Reading.** At 70 GB the room beyond the GPU's copy is 44K tokens. Rules 2 and 4 move that room between early reads
  and arrived turns; they do not make more of it, and what the early reads gain is taken back by the bumps. Whether
  they pay where there is room to stage (a larger host pool) is not tested: the 100 GB arms queued are the no-hint
  rival and the two JIT arms.

**Figures: `results/compare_c26_designs/` redrawn with `ec_full`** (`figs_designs.sh`, 94 s; 53 files): a seventh series,
dotted orange, in every figure, its own timeline and paired CDFs, and a ninth row in the wait split. The 43 files of
the other runs came out byte-identical. `plot_pricing_vs_jit.py` now picks the legend's column count so that it ends
inside the figure (seven labels ran past the right edge in three columns; two here); the 128-user figure, the
`compare_c26_ec` one and the six-series one redraw to the byte with it.
- `fq90` booted with its settings at 23:54Z (just-in-time, landing quantile 0.9, next-use eviction; no tracebacks, no
  client errors) and ends about 01:56Z on 2026-11-13.
EOF
tail -n 5 results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md | cut -c1-120; wc -l results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md", "description": "Append the all-four-rules arm's entry to the campaign record"}

{"file_path": "/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/campaign26/checks/pin_hold.py", "content": """"Host memory held by read pins, split by whether the read started before its turn arrived.
From agent_cache/:  nice -n 10 python3 -I -B results/campaign26/checks/pin_hold.py label=run [label=run ...]
Per run, from server.log's srs_pin, srs_unpin and ntp_arrive lines: every pin is paired with the next unpin of the same
turn and counted as tokens x seconds held. An early pin is one taken before its turn arrived; its hold is split at the
arrival into the wait for the turn and the wait in the queue. The mean level is all token-seconds over the span from the
first to the last pin event. Times are seconds; quantiles are p10 p50 p90."""
import collections, datetime as dt, re, sys

EVT = re.compile(r"^\[(.{23})\] HICACHE_EVT (srs_pin|srs_unpin|ntp_arrive) rid=\S+?-c(\d+)-t(\d+) (.*)")
TOKENS = re.compile(r"tokens=(\d+)")
REASON = re.compile(r"reason=(\w+)")
stamp = lambda s: dt.datetime.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f").replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc).timestamp()
q = lambda v, p: sorted(v)[min(len(v) - 1, int(p * len(v)))] if v else float("nan")
three = lambda v: f"{q(v, .1):.1f} {q(v, .5):.1f} {q(v, .9):.1f}"

for name, run in (a.split("=") for a in sys.argv[1:]):
    arrive, open_pins, holds, first, last = {}, {}, [], None, None
    for line in open(f"results/{run}/server.log", errors="replace"):
        m = EVT.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        t, kind, key = stamp(m.group(1)), m.group(2), (int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4)))
        if kind == "ntp_arrive":
            arrive[key] = t
            continue
        first, last = first or t, t
        if kind == "srs_pin":
            open_pins[key] = (t, int(TOKENS.search(m.group(5)).group(1)))
        elif key in open_pins:
            at, tokens = open_pins.pop(key)
            holds.append((key, at, t, tokens, REASON.search(m.group(5)).group(1)))
    span = last - first
    # A pin whose turn never arrived (the session ended, or the run did) was early for its whole hold.
    early = [h for h in holds if h[1] < arrive.get(h[0], float("inf"))]
    late = [h for h in holds if h[1] >= arrive.get(h[0], float("inf"))]
    area = lambda hs: sum(tokens * (end - at) for _, at, end, tokens, _ in hs)
    before = sum(tokens * (min(end, arrive.get(key, end)) - at) for key, at, end, tokens, _ in early)
    waits = [arrive[key] - at for key, at, _, _, _ in early if key in arrive and arrive[key] <= _ended(key, holds) if False] if False else \
        [min(end, arrive.get(key, end)) - at for key, at, end, _, _ in early]
    reasons = collections.Counter(h[4] for h in early)
    print(f"{name} {run}")
    print(f"  pins {len(holds)} paired ({len(open_pins)} still held at the end), mean level {area(holds) / span:,.0f} tokens over {span / 60:.0f} min")
    print(f"  early pins {len(early)} on {len({h[0] for h in early})} turns: {three([h[3] for h in early])} tokens; held before the arrival {three(waits)} s, "
          f"over 30 s {sum(w > 30 for w in waits)}, over 120 s {sum(w > 120 for w in waits)}; ended by " + ", ".join(f"{k} {n}" for k, n in reasons.most_common()))
    print(f"    token-seconds: before the arrival {before / 1e6:,.1f} M ({before / span:,.0f} tokens of the mean level), after it {(area(early) - before) / 1e6:,.1f} M ({(area(early) - before) / span:,.0f})")
    print(f"  pins taken at or after the arrival {len(late)}: held {three([h[2] - h[1] for h in late])} s; token-seconds {area(late) / 1e6:,.1f} M ({area(late) / span:,.0f} tokens of the mean level)")
"}

{"file_path": "/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/campaign26/checks/pin_hold.py", "content": """"Host memory held by read pins, split by whether the read landed before its turn arrived.
From agent_cache/:  nice -n 10 python3 -I -B results/campaign26/checks/pin_hold.py label=run [label=run ...]
Per run, from server.log's srs_pin, srs_unpin and ntp_arrive lines: every pin is paired with the next unpin of the same
turn and counted as tokens x seconds held. An early pin is one held over EARLY s before its turn arrived (to its unpin
when the turn never came); its hold is split at the arrival into the wait for the turn and the wait in the queue. The
mean level is all token-seconds over the span from the first to the last pin event, and each part's share of it is
printed in tokens. Times are seconds; quantiles are p10 p50 p90."""
import collections, datetime as dt, re, sys

EVT = re.compile(r"^\[(.{23})\] HICACHE_EVT (srs_pin|srs_unpin|ntp_arrive) rid=\S+?-c(\d+)-t(\d+) (.*)")
TOKENS = re.compile(r"tokens=(\d+)")
REASON = re.compile(r"reason=(\w+)")
stamp = lambda s: dt.datetime.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f").replace(tzinfo=dt.timezone.utc).timestamp()
q = lambda v, p: sorted(v)[min(len(v) - 1, int(p * len(v)))] if v else float("nan")
three = lambda v: f"{q(v, .1):.1f} {q(v, .5):.1f} {q(v, .9):.1f}"
EARLY = 0.05  # s; a read at arrival logs its pin within a few ms of the arrival line, on either side

for name, run in (a.split("=") for a in sys.argv[1:]):
    arrive, open_pins, holds, first, last = {}, {}, [], None, None
    for line in open(f"results/{run}/server.log", errors="replace"):
        m = EVT.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        t, kind, key = stamp(m.group(1)), m.group(2), (int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4)))
        if kind == "ntp_arrive":
            arrive[key] = t
            continue
        first, last = first or t, t
        if kind == "srs_pin":
            open_pins[key] = (t, int(TOKENS.search(m.group(5)).group(1)))
        elif key in open_pins:
            at, tokens = open_pins.pop(key)
            holds.append((key, at, t, tokens, REASON.search(m.group(5)).group(1)))
    span = last - first
    # Seconds a pin was held before its turn arrived; negative when it was taken after the arrival.
    wait = lambda h: min(h[2], arrive.get(h[0], h[2])) - h[1]
    early = [h for h in holds if wait(h) > EARLY]
    late = [h for h in holds if wait(h) <= EARLY]
    area = lambda hs: sum(tokens * (end - at) for _, at, end, tokens, _ in hs)
    before = sum(h[3] * wait(h) for h in early)
    waits = [wait(h) for h in early]
    reasons = collections.Counter(h[4] for h in early)
    print(f"{name} {run}")
    print(f"  pins {len(holds)} paired ({len(open_pins)} still held at the end), mean level {area(holds) / span:,.0f} tokens over {span / 60:.0f} min")
    print(f"  early pins {len(early)} on {len({h[0] for h in early})} turns: {three([h[3] for h in early])} tokens; held before the arrival {three(waits)} s, "
          f"over 30 s {sum(w > 30 for w in waits)}, over 120 s {sum(w > 120 for w in waits)}; ended by " + ", ".join(f"{k} {n}" for k, n in reasons.most_common()))
    print(f"    token-seconds: before the arrival {before / 1e6:,.1f} M ({before / span:,.0f} tokens of the mean level), after it {(area(early) - before) / 1e6:,.1f} M ({(area(early) - before) / span:,.0f})")
    print(f"  the other pins {len(late)}: held {three([h[2] - h[1] for h in late])} s; token-seconds {area(late) / 1e6:,.1f} M ({area(late) / span:,.0f} tokens of the mean level)")
"}

{"command": "cd /home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache; cat >> results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md <<'EOF'

**`fq90` (done 01:56Z on 2026-11-13, clean, GPU unit `GPU-6374d407`): timing just-in-time reads to land at the gap's p90
instead of its p10 takes three-quantile hints from 1.35-1.60 s to 0.94 s, still behind every leading run; its early
reads hold five times the host room that rule 1's do.** Tables: `compare_ec.out` (19 runs), `pairs_ec_ctl.out` (19
runs; earlier `pairs_ec_ctl_18runs.out`), `pairs_ec_fq90.out` (the 11 leading runs and this one, 10,830 turns),
`stall_ec_fq90.out`, `checks/latency_lead13.out`, `checks/pin_hold.out` (new check `checks/pin_hold.py`). One run of
this arm. It differs from the JIT p50 arm (`jit_p50_d`) and from rule 1 alone (`ec_r1`) in the read timing only: same
build, same next-use eviction, same hints.

| 6,715 shared returning turns | JIT p50 (lands at p10) | `fq90` (lands at p90) | rule 1 | rules 1, 3 | no gap forecast | no hints | JIT exact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean TTFT | 1.60, 1.35, 1.48 s | 0.94 s | 0.67 s | 0.66, 0.78 s | 0.69, 0.80 s | 0.71, 0.72 s | 0.51, 0.54 s |
| in the two load episodes | 5.24, 4.01, 4.33 s | 2.71 s | 1.75 s | 1.56, 2.31 s | 1.83, 2.21 s | 1.85, 1.84 s | 1.14, 1.31 s |
| turns over 10 s | 246, 172, 183 | 98 | 55 | 30, 93 | 53, 66 | 25, 47 | 14, 27 |
| recomputed tokens per turn | 970, 928, 1,007 | 446 | 181 | 214, 253 | 131, 193 | 145, 135 | 120, 151 |
| SSD pages, whole run | 563K, 580K, 569K | 506K | 448K | 437K, 415K | 469K, 482K | 562K, 559K | 388K, 397K |
| reads staged before arrival | 2,094, 2,202, 2,149 | 613 | 670 | 629, 560 | 0 | 0 | 1,202, 1,207 |
| mean tokens pinned by reads | 30.2K, 31.5K, 28.8K | 15.3K | 4.8K | 4.2K, 4.6K | 2.6K, 2.4K | 2.5K, 2.5K | 5.9K, 6.0K |
| turns sent before minute 115 | 10,043, 10,208, 10,050 | 11,204 | 11,580 | 11,690, 11,527 | 11,710, 11,654 | 11,680, 11,645 | 11,699, 11,703 |

- **Clean.** 11,740 turns in the 2 h, no client errors, no tracebacks, settings as queued (just-in-time, landing
  quantile 0.9, next-use eviction, no price learning, no soft pins). The engine times such a read past the p50 on
  purpose (`early_s` negative, plan expiry and read deadline moved with it). Decode, first-turn prefill and SSD speed in
  line with the other arms (36.2 ms per step at 8-15 running, 0.090 ms per token, 2.30 ms per page).
- **Against landing at the p10: 0.41-0.66 s faster in all three pairs** (5 % to 95 % clear of zero in each), where the
  three JIT p50 runs differ among themselves by up to 0.25 s. In the episodes 2.7 s against 4.0-5.2 s, half the
  recompute, and about 1,000-1,160 more turns before minute 115. One run of this arm, so by the repeat rule it is not
  counted as shown; it is the largest move between two settings of one knob in the campaign.
- **Against the leading runs: behind all eleven.** On the 6,715 turns by 0.14-0.29 s (rules, no gap forecast, no
  hints) and 0.40-0.43 s (exact hints), every interval clear of zero. That set ends in the first load episode. On the
  10,830 turns it shares with the leading runs alone: 0.97 s against 0.78-0.92 s and 0.71, 0.78 s (exact), behind by
  0.05-0.20 and 0.19-0.26 s, with two of the eleven intervals clear of zero and a third touching it; outside the
  episodes ten of eleven are (0.04-0.14 s). Rule 1 alone, the arm that differs in timing only: ahead by 0.27 s on the
  6,715 (-0.50 to -0.09) and by 0.09 s on the 10,830 (-0.31 to +0.12), one run each.
- **Latency and throughput: between the two groups.** 12.99 s per turn on the 9,716 turns shared with the leading runs
  and `jit_p50_d` (leading 12.00-12.61 s, `jit_p50_d` 16.24 s); 11,204 turns before minute 115 (leading
  11,446-11,710).
- **Why: its early reads sit on the room** (`checks/pin_hold.out`; an early pin is one held before its turn arrived).
  It lands about as many reads early as rule 1, 419 against 367, but they wait longer for their turn: p90 60 s against
  12 s, 75 over 30 s against 13, and 82 end with the turn never coming against 32. Before arrival they hold 13.2K
  tokens on average, of 44K of room, against 2.7K (rules 1 and 3: 2.4K and 2.0K; exact hints 4.0K with 864 early
  pins, none over 30 s; landing at the p10 24.6K with 1,182, 160 over 30 s). The room they hold is refused to the
  reads of turns that have arrived: 625 launches refused against 396, and 446 tokens recomputed per turn against 181.
  On the 9,716 turns of `stall_ec_fq90.out` its read stall equals rule 1's (0.29 and 0.30 s per turn); the difference
  is after admission (0.50 against 0.44 s).
- **Reading.** A fixed quantile cannot tell a read whose turn is about to come from one whose turn is a minute out or
  not coming. Moving it from the p10 to the p90 halves the room held and removes 0.41-0.66 s of the 0.68-0.93 s by
  which landing at the p10 trails rule 1; the expected-cost start gets the rest by holding a fifth of the room for
  about the same number of early reads. That is the deck's argument for rule 1 seen in a run, with the size of the
  edge over the better fixed quantile tried at 0.09-0.27 s on one run each. Against the rivals that start no read
  early it changes nothing: they hold no room before arrival and stand where rule 1 does.
- `ec_r3` booted with its settings at 01:57Z (just-in-time landing at the p10, return chance with a 30 s horizon; no
  tracebacks, no client errors) and ends about 03:59Z.
EOF
tail -n 5 results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md | cut -c1-200; wc -l results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md", "description": "Append the fq90 entry to the campaign record"}

import re, sys
s = sys.argv[1]
def cells(path):
    """Section title -> {(row, column): cell text}, and the per-arm rows."""
    out, rows, sec, cols = {}, {}, None, None
    for line in open(path):
        line = line.rstrip("\n")
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if not line.startswith(" "):
            sec, cols = re.sub(r"\d+ returning turns shared by.*", "shared", line.split(";")[0]), None
            continue
        parts = line.split()
        if cols is None and not re.search(r"\d", line):
            cols = parts
            continue
        if cols is None:
            rows[(sec, parts[0])] = " ".join(parts[1:])
            continue
        vals = re.findall(r"[+-][\d.]+ \[[^\]]*\]", line)
        for c, v in zip(cols, vals):
            out[(sec, parts[0], c)] = v
    return out, rows
(o, orow), (n, nrow) = cells("results/campaign26/pairs_ec_ctl.out"), cells(f"{s}/pairs_ec_ctl_20runs.out")

badrow = [(k, v, nrow.get(k)) for k, v in orow.items() if nrow.get(k) != v]
print(f"old cells {len(o)}, new cells {len(n)}, old cells changed or missing {len(bad)}; old rows {len(orow)}, new rows {len(nrow)}, changed {len(badrow)}")
for b in bad[:8] + badrow[:8]:

  tracebacks, no client errors) and ends about 03:59Z.

**`ec_r3` (done 03:58Z on 2026-11-13, clean, GPU unit `GPU-6374d407`): rule 3 alone leaves JIT p50 where it was, 1.48 s
against 1.35-1.60 s; the gain of the pricing arms is rule 1's.** Tables: `compare_ec.out` (20 runs),
`pairs_ec_ctl.out` (20 runs; earlier `pairs_ec_ctl_19runs.out`), `pairs_ec_r3.out` (this run and the three JIT p50
runs, 9,690 turns), `stall_ec_designs.out`, `checks/latency_r3.out`, `checks/pin_hold.out` (eight runs). One run of this
arm. It differs from the JIT p50 arm (`jit_p50_d`) in the eviction rule only, chance of return within 30 s from the
three quantiles instead of next use from the p50: same build, same just-in-time reads landing at the p10, same hints.
With `ec_r1` and `ec_r13` it completes the two-by-two of rules 1 and 3.

| 6,715 shared returning turns | neither rule (JIT p50) | rule 3 alone (`ec_r3`) | rule 1 alone | rules 1, 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean TTFT | 1.60, 1.35, 1.48 s | 1.48 s | 0.67 s | 0.66, 0.78 s |
| in the two load episodes | 5.24, 4.01, 4.33 s | 4.23 s | 1.75 s | 1.56, 2.31 s |
| turns over 10 s | 246, 172, 183 | 186 | 55 | 30, 93 |
| recomputed tokens per turn | 970, 928, 1,007 | 1,042 | 181 | 214, 253 |
| SSD pages, whole run | 563K, 580K, 569K | 540K | 448K | 437K, 415K |
| tokens evicted, GPU / host (M) | 62.4 / 52.3, 63.4 / 53.5, 63.5 / 52.4 | 60.6 / 51.0 | 52.4 / 40.5 | 51.4 / 39.6, 50.1 / 38.4 |
| reads staged before arrival | 2,094, 2,202, 2,149 | 2,207 | 670 | 629, 560 |
| mean tokens pinned by reads | 30.2K, 31.5K, 28.8K | 32.0K | 4.8K | 4.2K, 4.6K |
| turns sent before minute 115 | 10,043, 10,208, 10,050 | 10,058 | 11,580 | 11,690, 11,527 |

- **Clean.** 10,409 turns in the 2 h, no client errors, no tracebacks, settings as queued (just-in-time landing at the
  p10, return chance with a 30 s horizon, no price learning, no soft pins). Decode and first-turn prefill in line with
  the other arms (36.1 ms per step at 8-15 running, 0.089 ms per token); SSD 2.61 ms per page in its 83 large reads
  against 2.47-2.50 for the JIT p50 runs.
- **Rule 3 without rule 1: no effect on TTFT.** Against the three JIT p50 runs -0.12, +0.13 and +0.00 s on the 6,715
  turns, and -0.04, +0.09 and -0.02 s on the 9,690 turns the four runs share. Five of the six intervals include zero;
  the sixth, against the fastest JIT p50 run on the 6,715, has this arm slower (+0.01 to +0.28). Against `jit_p50_d`,
  the run that differs in the rule alone: +0.004 s (-0.11 to +0.12) and -0.019 s (-0.13 to +0.09). The three JIT p50
  runs differ among themselves by up to 0.25 s. Latency 16.10 s per turn against 15.59-16.19 s, and 10,058 turns before
  minute 115 against 10,043-10,208. The wait splits part for part like `jit_p50_d`'s on the 7,283 turns of the figure
  set: 1.48 = 0.39 read stall + 0.38 rest of the queue wait + 0.71 after admission, against 1.49 = 0.38 + 0.42 + 0.69.
- **Rule 3 with rule 1: no effect either** (earlier runs): rules 1 and 3 against rule 1 alone -0.02 s (-0.06 to
  +0.03) and +0.10 s (-0.02 to +0.32). **Rule 1 is worth the same in both columns:** 0.68-0.93 s under next-use
  eviction (`ec_r1` against the three JIT p50 runs) and 0.71-0.83 s under return chance (rules 1 and 3 against this
  run), every interval clear of zero.
- **SSD traffic: perhaps a few percent less.** 4-7 % fewer pages than each JIT p50 run on every set (540K against
  563-580K in the whole run; 533K against 554-564K on the 9,690 turns, where the three JIT p50 runs span 1.8 %), with
  3-5 % fewer tokens evicted. With rule 1 on, the whole-run counts of rules 1 and 3 are 2-7 % under rule 1's, and on
  the shared turns they are level with it (254K, 251K against 251K). One run here.
- **Why: the eviction rule cannot reach what costs** (`checks/pin_hold.out`). The reads still land at the p10 and
  wait for their turn: 1,175 early pins against 1,182 for `jit_p50_d`, held 45 s at the p90 against 41 s, holding
  27.9K tokens before arrival against 24.6K, of 44K of room. Pinned memory is outside any eviction score, so the reads
  of turns that have arrived are refused that room as before (1,871 launches refused against 1,732-1,761) and the turns
  recompute as before.
- **Reading.** The two-by-two is complete: the 0.7-0.9 s between JIT p50 and the pricing arms is the read start (rule
  1), in both columns; the eviction score moves TTFT in neither row. It joins the earlier result that four eviction
  scores are level once reads hold little room: next use from the p50 (`ec_r1` 0.67 s), chance of return (0.66,
  0.78 s), ended first then LRU (`nofc` 0.69, 0.80 s), queued turns only (`nofc_noend` 0.71, 0.72 s). At this setting
  rule 3 is not a source of the TTFT gain; what is left for it to show is the SSD traffic, and that needs a repeat.
- Figures: `compare_c26_designs/` redrawn at 04:04Z. `timeline_ec_r3.png` is new and `ec_wait_split.png` has the arm's
  row; every other figure and table of the set is byte-identical (`pricing_vs_jit.pdf` is re-saved, its PNG and CSV
  unchanged).
- `nofc_c128` booted with its settings at 04:00Z (128 users, 160 GB host pool, reads at arrival, return chance with
  score `lru`; no tracebacks, no client errors) and ends about 06:02Z."}

{"file_path": "/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/campaign26/checks/watch_all.sh", "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bash
# c26_ec/watch.sh with its problem checks widened to every host pool size (that one skips run folders ending in
# _H100, so the three 100 GB arms ran unchecked). From agent_cache/, on the host:  bash results/campaign26/checks/watch_all.sh
# Exits on the next arm's end in campaign 26's launcher.log or on a problem: a traceback in the running server's log,
# client errors, a client that stops writing for 300 s, or the container down.
L=results/campaign26/launcher.log
P='C26 .*(DONE|STOP|IDLE)'
n0=$(grep -cE "$P" "$L")
while :; do
  n=$(grep -cE "$P" "$L")
  if [ "$n" -gt "$n0" ]; then echo "launcher: $(grep -E "$P" "$L" | tail -1 | cut -c1-240)"; exit 0; fi
  R=$(cat results/.current_run 2>/dev/null)
  case "$R" in *_NAT160|*custom_L1nat_H*)
    if [ -f "results/$R/server.log" ]; then
      tb=$(grep -ac 'Traceback' "results/$R/server.log")
      [ "$tb" -gt 0 ] && { echo "ALERT: $tb tracebacks in results/$R/server.log"; exit 0; }
    fi
    for c in results/$R/client_*/client.jsonl; do
      [ -f "$c" ] || continue
      e=$(grep -ac '"error": "' "$c")
      [ "$e" -gt 0 ] && { echo "ALERT: $e client errors in $c"; exit 0; }
      age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$c") ))
      [ "$age" -gt 300 ] && { echo "ALERT: $c has not grown for $age s"; exit 0; }
    done ;;
  esac
  docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -q '^sglang_hicache$' || { echo "ALERT: container down"; exit 0; }
  sleep 60
done
"}

EOF

{"command": "cd /home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache; S=/tmp/claude-1001/-home-wanhr-sglang/7c93b1d5-dc1c-431d-8d3e-efb4ae23a30d/scratchpad; for f in compare_ec_h100cut pairs_ec_h100cut stall_ec_h100cut; do [ -e results/campaign26/$f.out ] && echo "EXISTS $f" || cp $S/$f.out results/campaign26/$f.out; done; [ -e results/campaign26/checks/latency_h100cut.out ] && echo EXISTS || cp $S/latency_h100cut.out results/campaign26/checks/latency_h100cut.out; ls -la results/campaign26/*h100cut* results/campaign26/checks/*h100cut* | awk '{print $5, $9}'; cat >> results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md <<'EOF'

**`nofc_noend_h100_cut` (the 84 min before the outage, GPU unit `GPU-6374d407`): with a 100 GB host pool the rival
with no hints reads from SSD on 0.7 % of returning turns and reaches 0.37 s, ahead of JIT exact at 70 GB (0.48,
0.51 s).** Tables: `compare_ec_h100cut.out` (ten runs), `pairs_ec_h100cut.out`, `stall_ec_h100cut.out`,
`checks/latency_h100cut.out` (seven runs on the 8,030 returning turns they share: the cut run's first 79 min, which
hold the first load episode and not the second). One run, cut; the rerun in progress is its repeat.

| 8,030 shared returning turns | no hints, 100 GB (cut) | no hints, 70 GB | rules 1, 3, 70 GB | JIT exact, 70 GB |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mean TTFT | 0.37 s | 0.65, 0.66 s | 0.60, 0.70 s | 0.48, 0.51 s |
| in the first load episode (1,453 turns) | 0.51 s | 1.77, 1.77 s | 1.52, 2.21 s | 1.12, 1.25 s |
| elsewhere (6,577 turns) | 0.34 s | 0.41, 0.41 s | 0.40, 0.37 s | 0.34, 0.34 s |
| p99; turns over 10 s | 2.6 s; 0 | 7.2 s; 25 and 7.9 s; 47 | 6.8 s; 29 and 10.4 s; 94 | 5.0 s; 15 and 6.1 s; 27 |
| read stall + rest of queue wait + after admission | 0.006 + 0.019 + 0.346 | 0.223 + 0.053 + 0.376, 0.230 + 0.060 + 0.367 | 0.141 + 0.072 + 0.390, 0.190 + 0.116 + 0.400 | 0.070 + 0.045 + 0.366, 0.072 + 0.052 + 0.383 |
| turns reading from SSD | 56 | 1,125, 1,138 | 991, 1,006 | 691, 743 |
| SSD pages | 17K | 329K, 328K | 266K, 258K | 210K, 223K |
| recomputed tokens per turn | 34 | 127, 118 | 179, 217 | 106, 131 |
| turn latency | 10.72 s | 11.35, 11.32 s | 11.52, 11.87 s | 11.26, 11.27 s |

- **Clean to the cut.** 8,800 turns in 83.7 min, no client errors, no tracebacks. Decode 36.3 ms per step at 8-15
  running and first-turn prefill 0.089 ms per token, in line with the other arms.
- **Almost nothing is read.** 56 of the 8,030 returning turns read from SSD against 1,125 and 1,138 for the same arm
  at 70 GB; host eviction 7.5 M tokens in 79 min against 47 M in 115 min; no read launch refused room; 396K tokens of
  room idle at the price updates against 76K. The sessions not parked in a long gap hold up to about 1,010K tokens in
  the first episode (`load K` in the position table), just under the pool's 1,017K.
- **TTFT.** 0.28 and 0.29 s under the same arm at 70 GB (intervals -0.48 to -0.11), 1.26 s under it in the episode.
  0.11 and 0.14 s under JIT exact at 70 GB (+0.02 to +0.26), all of it in the episode (0.61 and 0.74 s; elsewhere
  0.00). No turn over 10 s.
- **The wait.** The read stall is 0.006 s per turn (0.22-0.23 s at 70 GB, 0.07 s for JIT exact there). That is all a
  read-start rule could take off at this pool size: the two JIT arms queued at 100 GB can lead this arm by a few
  hundredths of a second at most, unless their eviction order costs or saves reads.
- **Latency.** 0.54-0.63 s per turn under the 70 GB leaders, more than the TTFT gap: the time after the first token
  is 0.3-0.4 s shorter as well.
- **Reading.** At 44 users, 30 GB more host memory removes the reads themselves, with no hint: the larger pool does
  not make room for earlier reads, it leaves almost none to start. Read-start rules have something to decide only
  where the pool is well under the working load (70 GB here).
- **Limits.** One run, its first 79 min. The second episode carries a higher load (about 1,050K tokens in the 70 GB
  runs, above the pool), so the full run should read more there.
EOF
wc -l results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md", "description": "Install the cut-run tables and record the result"}

{"file_path": "/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/results/campaign26/checks/limits/pool_sweep.py", "content": """"Host-pool sweep on recorded timelines: the share of returning turns that read from SSD as the host pool grows.
From agent_cache/:  nice -n 10 python3 -I -B results/campaign26/checks/limits/pool_sweep.py | tee results/campaign26/checks/limits/pool_sweep.out
Uses the one-pool model of frozen/ec_policy_20261111/evict_replay/evict_replay.py, with its limits: no pins, no GPU and
host split, the run's own timeline, so it gives read shares and not TTFT. The model's pool M is fitted once, on a 70 GB
run, so that LRU gives that run's measured share. Another host size moves M in one of two ways, since the fit does not
say which: by the same ratio as the host pool, or by the same number of tokens. The 100 GB cut run is the check."""
import os

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
source = open(os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "..", "..", "frozen", "ec_policy_20261111", "evict_replay", "evict_replay.py")).read()
ns = {"__name__": "evict_replay_model"}
exec(compile(source[:source.index('\nif len(sys.argv) > 1 and sys.argv[1] == "noend":')], "evict_replay.py", "exec"), ns)
load, simulate, share = ns["load"], ns["simulate"], ns["share"]
POLICIES = (("LRU", ns["lru"]), ("LRU, ended sessions first", ns["lru_end"]), ("next use from the p50", ns["next_use"]()),
            ("return chance within 30 s", ns["return_chance"](30, ns["chance_own"])), ("exact next use", ns["exact"]))

TOKENS_PER_GB = 10172.8  # host pool tokens per GB: 1,017,280 at 100 GB, 1,627,648 at 160 GB
FIT = ("nofc_noend_rep", "20261112_174138_three_tier_wc_oracle_v2_nu_owned_custom_L1nat_H70", 70, 0.170)
CHECK = ("nofc_noend_h100_cut", "20261113_060157_three_tier_wc_oracle_v2_nu_owned_custom_L1nat_H100", 100, 56 / 8030)
SIZES = (70, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100, 110, 120, 136, 160)


def fit(turns, target):
    """The pool at which LRU reads on the target share of returning turns."""
    lo, hi = 200_000, 3_000_000
    for _ in range(18):
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if share(simulate(turns, mid, ns["lru"])) > target:
            lo = mid
        else:
            hi = mid
    return hi


def pools(m70, gb):
    """M at a host pool of gb GB: scaled by ratio, and moved by the tokens added."""
    return int(m70 * gb / 70), int(m70 + (gb - 70) * TOKENS_PER_GB)


name, run, gb, target = FIT
turns = load(run)
m70 = fit(turns, target)
print(f"fit on {name} ({gb} GB, measured {100 * target:.1f} % of returning turns reading from SSD): {len(turns)} turns, M = {m70:,} tokens "
      f"(the host pool is {int(gb * TOKENS_PER_GB):,})")

cname, crun, cgb, cshare = CHECK
cturns = load(crun)
by_ratio, by_tokens = pools(m70, cgb)
print(f"\ncheck on {cname}'s own timeline ({cgb} GB, {len(cturns)} turns, measured {100 * cshare:.1f} %): LRU share with M by ratio ({by_ratio:,}) "
      f"{100 * share(simulate(cturns, by_ratio, ns['lru'])):.1f} %, by tokens ({by_tokens:,}) {100 * share(simulate(cturns, by_tokens, ns['lru'])):.1f} %")
# The same window of the 70 GB run, so the two timelines can be told apart from the two pool sizes.
t_cut = max(r["t_send"] for r in cturns)
head = [r for r in turns if r["t_send"] <= t_cut]
print(f"  the 70 GB run's first {t_cut / 60:.0f} min ({len(head)} turns) at those pools: {100 * share(simulate(head, by_ratio, ns['lru'])):.1f} %, "
      f"{100 * share(simulate(head, by_tokens, ns['lru'])):.1f} %; at its own M {100 * share(simulate(head, m70, ns['lru'])):.1f} %")

for how, pick in (("M scaled by the host pool's ratio", 0), ("M moved by the tokens added", 1)):
    print(f"\n{name}'s timeline, {how}: share of returning turns reading from SSD (K tokens read per returning turn)")
    print(f"  {'host GB':>8s} {'M':>10s} | " + " | ".join(f"{label:>26s}" for label, _ in POLICIES))
    for size in SIZES:
        m = pools(m70, size)[pick]
        cells = []
        for _, prio in POLICIES:
            o = simulate(turns, m, prio)
            cells.append(f"{100 * share(o):17.1f} % ({o['read_tokens'] / o['returning'] / 1000:5.2f})")
        print(f"  {size:8d} {m:10,d} | " + " | ".join(cells))
"}

**Host-pool sweep on the eviction replay (CPU, `checks/limits/pool_sweep.py` and `.out`): the reads fade by about half
for every 5 GB above 70 GB, and the model fitted at 70 GB gives the 100 GB run's 0.7 %.** The one-pool model of
`frozen/ec_policy_20261111/evict_replay/` (no pins, no GPU and host split, a run's own timeline; read shares, not
TTFT), fitted on `nofc_noend_rep` so that LRU gives its measured 17.0 % of returning turns reading from SSD. Another
host size moves the model's pool by the host pool's ratio or by the tokens added; both are shown, as a range.

| Host pool | 70 GB | 75 | 80 | 85 | 90 | 100 | 110 | 160 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LRU (no hints) | 17.0 % | 9.4-10.8 | 4.9-6.7 | 2.7-4.2 | 1.5-2.7 | 0.8-1.2 | 0.6-0.8 | 0.2-0.3 |
| LRU, ended sessions first | 13.7 % | 6.7-8.0 | 3.0-4.4 | 1.3-2.4 | 0.6-1.3 | 0.0-0.3 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| next use from the p50 | 15.5 % | 9.1-10.5 | 4.5-6.6 | 2.2-3.9 | 1.5-2.1 | 0.8-1.1 | 0.6-0.8 | 0.2-0.3 |
| exact next use | 9.1 % | 4.8-5.5 | 2.1-3.3 | 0.9-1.7 | 0.4-0.9 | 0.1-0.2 | 0.0-0.1 | 0.0 |

- **Check.** On the 100 GB cut run's own timeline the model gives 0.7 % (by ratio) and 0.9 % (by tokens); measured
  0.7 %. The 70 GB run's first 84 min give 0.7-0.8 % at those pools and 12.6 % at 70 GB, so the fall is the pool's
  and not the timeline's.
- **What a forecast can save in reads shrinks with the pool:** exact next use against LRU is 7.9 points of returning
  turns at 70 GB, about 5 at 75 GB, 3 at 80 GB, 2 at 85 GB and under 1 from 100 GB.
- **Reading.** 70 GB, the smallest pool that still mirrors the GPU, is the setting most favourable to hints at 44
  users; a pool between 70 and 100 GB would show a smaller version of the 70 GB result, and a pool above 100 GB (the
  136 GB arm once proposed) next to nothing. Not queued. A setting with more reads and a short GPU queue would need
  more users per GB without the GPU saturating; the model cannot place it, since it replays one run's timeline.
EOF
wc -l results/campaign26/DECISIONS.md", "description": "Save the pool sweep and record it"}

{"file_path": "/home/wanhr/sglang/agent_cache/frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c26_ec/figs_designs_h100.sh", "content": "#!/bin/bash
# Redraws results/compare_c26_designs_h100: 44 users, 0.1 users/s, a 100 GB host pool against 70 GB; the rival with no
# hints, JIT p50 and JIT exact, one run each per pool size. From the host:
#   docker exec sglang_hicache bash /sgl-workspace/sglang/agent_cache/frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c26_ec/figs_designs_h100.sh
# A 100 GB arm joins once it is in results/campaign26/manifest.txt; the run cut by the outage keeps its own timeline.
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=/sgl-workspace/sglang/agent_cache
HERE=$ROOT/frozen/oracle_scripts_staging/c26_ec
OUT=results/compare_c26_designs_h100
# No GPU for the plots: a campaign may be running on it.
export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 FIGSET=designs_h100 PYTHONPATH=$ROOT/scripts

cd $ROOT/scripts
nice -n 15 python3 -B $HERE/plot_timeline.py
nice -n 15 python3 -B $HERE/plot_pricing_vs_jit.py --set designs_h100 2> >(grep -v findfont >&2)
nice -n 15 python3 -B $HERE/plot_ec.py

cd $ROOT
ARMS=""
for arm in nofc_noend_rep nofc_noend_h100 jit_p50_d jit_p50_h100 jit_exact_d jit_exact_h100; do
    if grep -q "^$arm " results/campaign26/manifest.txt; then ARMS="$ARMS $arm"; fi
done
STALL_CSV=$OUT/ec_wait_split.csv nice -n 15 python3 -I -B $HERE/stall_ec.py $ARMS > results/campaign26/stall_ec_designs_h100.out
cd $ROOT/scripts
nice -n 15 python3 -B $HERE/plot_stall.py ../$OUT/ec_wait_split.csv
"}
